# Ezekiel 12 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 12:12 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-the-prince who [is] in-their-midst upon-[his]-shoulder shall-carry in-the-darkness, and-shall-go-out; through-the-wall they-shall-dig to-bring-out through-it; his-face he-shall-cover, so-that he-does-not-see with-[his]-eye the-ground. |
| LOGOS | And the prince who is among them shall lift his baggage upon his shoulder at dusk, and shall go out. They shall dig through the wall to bring things out through it. He shall cover his face, that he may not see the land with his eyes. |
| PNEUMA | Their prince will carry his belongings on his shoulder at dusk and leave through a hole dug in the wall. He will cover his face so he can't see the ground. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 12:13 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-I-will-spread My-net upon-him, and-he-shall-be-caught in-My-snare; and-I-will-bring-him to-Babylon, [the]-land-of the-Chaldeans, but-it he-shall-not-see, and-there he-shall-die. |
| LOGOS | And I will spread My net over him, and he shall be taken in My snare. And I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, yet he shall not see it, and he shall die there. |
| PNEUMA | But I will spread My net and catch him in My trap. I will bring him to Babylon in the land of the Chaldeans — but he will never see it. He will die there. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 12:4 (overlap: 4%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-bring-out your-vessels like-vessels-of exile by-day before-their-eyes, and-you shall-go-out in-the-evening before-their-eyes, like-goings-out-of exile. |
| LOGOS | You shall bring out your baggage by day in their sight, as baggage for exile, and you shall go out yourself at evening in their sight, as those do who must go into exile. |
| PNEUMA | Bring out your packed bags during the day where they can see. Then at evening, leave — the way people leave when they're going into exile, while they watch. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.
